questions.question: A 'Device' interface declares print(), scan(), and fax(), so a simple printer class is forced to implement scan() and fax() as empty stubs. Which SOLID principle does this fat interface violate?
questions.explanation: ISP says no client should depend on methods it does not use; split Device into IPrinter, IScanner, IFax so each implementor takes only what it needs.

questions.question: OrderService instantiates 'new MySQLOrderRepository()' directly, so swapping in a Mongo implementation means editing OrderService itself. Which SOLID principle says both should depend on an abstraction instead?
questions.explanation: DIP: high-level modules should not depend on low-level details - inject an IOrderRepository abstraction so concrete stores can be swapped freely.

questions.question: In an air-traffic-control model, planes never call each other directly; all landing requests and clearances route through a single control-tower object. Which pattern centralizes this communication?
questions.explanation: The Mediator pattern collects many-to-many colleague interactions into one object, turning a tangled web of references into star topology.

questions.question: A custom social graph stores friends in an internal adjacency structure that clients must not see, yet clients need to visit every friend one by one. Which pattern supplies that sequential access?
questions.explanation: Iterator exposes next()/hasNext() traversal while hiding the collection's internal representation - the client never touches the adjacency data.

questions.question: A game must snapshot a level's state so 'load checkpoint' restores it later, without exposing the Level class's internals to the save system. Which pattern captures and externalizes state this way?
questions.explanation: Memento hands out an opaque state token that only the originator can re-enter, preserving encapsulation while enabling restore/undo.

questions.question: When an order is placed, OrderService publishes an 'OrderPlaced' message; Inventory, Billing, and Notification each react independently with no direct calls between them. Which architectural style is this?
questions.explanation: In an event-driven style, producers emit events and consumers react asynchronously through a broker, keeping services decoupled.

questions.question: A file explorer must treat a single File and a Folder that itself holds files and subfolders identically - 'size()' should just work on both. Which pattern builds this part-whole tree?
questions.explanation: Composite gives leaf (File) and container (Folder) a common interface so clients treat individual objects and whole trees uniformly.

questions.question: An AST's node classes are stable, but the team must keep adding operations - pretty-print, type-check, code-gen - without editing the node classes each time. Which pattern puts each new operation in its own object?
questions.explanation: Visitor separates the operation from the structure: each new algorithm is a visitor class that double-dispatches across the fixed node types.

questions.question: An e-commerce platform does 100 reads per write, so the team splits the design: a denormalized read store optimized for queries, and a write model enforcing invariants - each scaled separately. Which pattern?
questions.explanation: CQRS segregates the write (command) model from the read (query) model so each can be scaled, cached, and shaped independently.

questions.question: Subclasses FlyingDuck, RubberDuck, and MuteDog multiply every time a behavior combination changes; the redesign instead gives each object swappable fly and quack behaviors. Which design principle guided the change?
questions.explanation: Composing behavior objects into the host avoids the subclass explosion that an inheritance hierarchy forces for every new combination.

questions.question: A text editor needs undo/redo support where each user action is stored and replayable. Which pattern encapsulates each action as an object?
questions.explanation: The Command pattern turns requests into objects, enabling history stacks for undo and redo operations.

questions.question: Module A directly reads and writes Module B's private variables instead of using its interface. Which type of coupling is this?
questions.explanation: Content coupling occurs when one module accesses or modifies another module's internal data — the strongest and worst coupling form.

questions.question: A utility module groups unrelated functions only because they all run at startup time. Which type of cohesion is this?
questions.explanation: Temporal cohesion groups elements solely because they execute at the same time, a relatively weak form of cohesion.

questions.question: A payment system must support new payment providers without editing existing checkout code. Which SOLID principle should guide the design?
questions.explanation: The Open-Closed Principle makes modules extensible without modification, e.g., via plugin interfaces for new payment providers.

questions.question: Each microservice owns its own database and exposes data only through APIs. Which microservices design pattern is this?
questions.explanation: Database per Service keeps each microservice's data private to its own database, enforcing loose coupling and autonomy.

questions.question: A game character must switch behavior entirely as it changes between walking, running, and flying modes at runtime, each behavior encapsulated in an object behind a common interface. Identify the pattern.
questions.explanation: The State pattern lets an object alter its behavior when its internal state changes; unlike Strategy (chosen algorithms), transitions are driven by the object's state.

questions.question: A support system passes each ticket down a linked sequence of handlers - agent, supervisor, manager - each either handling it or forwarding it. Identify the pattern.
questions.explanation: Chain of Responsibility decouples sender from receiver by passing a request along a handler chain until one handles it - matching the escalation scenario.

questions.question: A map editor renders millions of trees; shared mesh/texture data is stored once per tree type while position and scale are passed in per call. The pattern used to cut memory.
questions.explanation: Flyweight shares intrinsic state (texture, mesh) among many objects and passes extrinsic state (position, scale) per use, drastically reducing memory.

questions.question: Business logic depends only on abstract 'ports' (repositories, payment gateways); swappable adapters plug in Oracle, MongoDB, or mocks without the core knowing. Name the architecture.
questions.explanation: Hexagonal (Ports and Adapters) architecture isolates the domain core behind ports; external technologies connect through adapters that implement them.

questions.question: Square extends Rectangle; client code calls setWidth(5) then setHeight(3) expecting area 15 but gets 9 - substituting the subtype breaks expectations. Which SOLID principle is violated?
questions.explanation: LSP requires subtypes to be substitutable for their base types without breaking correctness; the classic Square-is-a-Rectangle example violates it.
